Great advice for every situation. :)

alias rm='rm -i'

doesn't work in all situations. The GNU version of rm honors the last of two mutually exclusive options. If you type

rm -rf foo/

it expands to 

rm -i -rf

and the -f overrides the -i.

People are taking the piss with those recommendations. Just alias rm to rm -i if you feel the need to although many systems have that by default. The system I admin has it in the system wide .bashrc file for all users because rm is a powerful command and needs to be treated with care.
